A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same dual-perspective NLG meta-evaluation study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments with 16 LLM judges on SummEval and Topical-Chat, human re-evaluation in Section 3, and benchmark validation in Appendix C.3.

after.justification: V2 retains the original LLM experiments and human studies and reports revised global meta-evaluation results using CEM.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 replaces linear weighted kappa with the Closeness Evaluation Measure (CEM) within the proposed global meta-evaluation procedure. This is a localized component change; local adjacent-pair comparison, error injection, and anchor-based benchmark construction remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SummEval summarization and Topical-Chat dialogue generation with the same quality aspects and global/local scenarios. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: the same 16 judges appear in the main comparisons, seven in the preliminary study, six in the anchor comparison, and 14 in the scoring-versus-comparison analysis. Pearson and Spearman remain the traditional comparison measures.

E3.justification: The primary global evaluation metric changes from linear weighted kappa to CEM in both the preliminary study and the constructed-benchmark evaluations. This substantially changes the basis of global performance assessment; the documented data selection, prompts, model configurations, and sampling settings are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: The human checks, anchor validation, confusion matrices, quality-gap analyses, and scoring-range comparisons are retained. The scoring-versus-direct-comparison analysis moves from v1 Table 10 to v2 Table 5 without changing its results.

E5.justification: Appendices A.3-A.4 retain ten-generation sampling and the same mean, mode, and order-swapped judgment aggregation. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting practices appear.

E6.justification: Global numerical results are replaced in Table 1 and in v1 Table 2 versus v2 Table 3. For example, DeepSeek-V3 changes from kappa 0.645, rank 8, to CEM 0.779, rank 10; Prometheus-2-8x7B moves from rank 10 to 8. These are different-metric results, not same-setting performance gains. Local results and human-validation outcomes remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 replaces the weighted-kappa definition, including linear disagreement weights and expected agreement, with the normalized CEM definition and its class-frequency-based logarithmic closeness function. This is a localized mathematical revision without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: complementary global/local evaluation capabilities, automatic benchmark construction without additional human annotation, and analysis of 16 LLM judges. The conclusion is unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly justifies CEM because it does not require equal intervals between adjacent categories, connecting the metric choice to the paper's criticism of averaging ordinal ratings. Interpretations of judge behavior, scoring-versus-comparison findings, and construction limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The introduction replaces a promised future code/data release with a statement of release and a concrete repository address. Section 4.2 also explicitly describes reference selection as similarity-based. Existing prompts, sampling details, benchmark statistics, and construction costs remain available.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds explicit comparisons with Perrella et al. (2024a) and Agrawal et al. (2024) on alternative MT meta-evaluation formulations. The introduction adds Sai et al. (2021) and He et al. (2023), while Cohen and Sakai references are removed with the kappa formulation. Amigo et al. (2020) was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: V2 clarifies the preliminary-study and construction descriptions, rewrites and expands related work, improves cross-references, and adds acknowledgements. The overall section and appendix organization remains substantially the same.

P2.justification: V2 adds main-text Table 2 by redisplaying the coherence example from the existing appendix and moves v1 Table 10 into the main text as Table 5. Captions and aspect abbreviations are clarified, with accompanying layout changes. The five figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: V2 better aligns its global-scoring rationale with its treatment of ratings as ordinal rather than equally spaced (Section 3.1 and Appendix A.2). Closer prior-work comparisons, a concrete code/data access link, and more accessible examples improve clarity and reproducibility information. These are limited quality gains; the larger global scores reflect a different metric, while the validation evidence remains unchanged.
